chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya Yahya from Ya'qub ibn Yazid from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah from whom he mentioned from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"Reciting with them is sufficient for you, equivalent to the recitation of the self [i.e., oneself]."
As for what the Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) mentioned regarding the choice between recitation and tasbih in the last two rak'ahs, that which he narrated indicates this:
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on recitation versus tasbih in the last two rak'ahs of prayer according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the juristic principle that reciting a portion of the Quran in the last two rak'ahs of certain prayers is sufficient to fulfill the obligation, equating it to the full recitation. It specifically addresses the scholarly debate regarding the permissibility of substituting Quranic recitation with *tasbih* (glorifications) in these rak'ahs, affirming that the Imam's practice supports this flexibility as a valid alternative rather than a lesser act.
